title: Spin-momentum locking of polariton edge states in honeycomb lattices
authors: Andrea Herrero Otermin, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Dheerendra Singh, Neha Bhoria, Rimi Banerjee, Christian Mayer, Simon Betzold, Siddhartha Dam, Monika Emmerling, Sven Höfling, Luis Viña, Subhaskar Mandal, Carlos Antón-Solanas
abstract: Transverse-electric/Transverse-magnetic splitting in dielectric-mirror microcavities introduces an effective spin-orbit coupling for photons. While the bulk states remain linearly polarized, for exponentially localized edge states in a photonic lattice, this coupling induces elliptical polarization whose handedness is locked to the propagation direction, analogous to the transverse spin of evanescent electromagnetic waves. We reveal spin-momentum locking through Stokes polarimetry of zigzag edge states in a honeycomb exciton-polariton lattice. The effect persists in a stretched honeycomb supporting a photonic bandgap, where spin-polarized carrier injection enables selective lasing of either chiral edge states. Our results provide a route toward ultrafast spin-controlled unidirectional propagation in polariton systems without external magnetic fields.
summary: The paper reports the experimental observation of spin-momentum locking (SML) in polariton edge states within honeycomb lattices. By exploiting the inherent spin-orbit coupling from cavity geometry, they demonstrate that counter-propagating edge modes carry opposite circular polarizations. This effect is leveraged to achieve all-optical control over light directionality via spin-selective lasing.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate spin-momentum locking (SML) of polariton edge states and achieve ultrafast, all-optical control over their directional propagation without external magnetic fields.
main_result: SML is confirmed in the zigzag edge states of honeycomb exciton-polariton lattices via polarization measurements. Furthermore, selective lasing using spin-polarized injection enables switching the direction of light flow by changing the pump helicity.
method: The study combines experimental characterization using micro-photoluminescence with full Stokes polarimetry and theoretical modeling based on effective Hamiltonian descriptions for photonic lattices.
model_or_system: The system is an exciton-polariton honeycomb lattice realized in GaAs-based semiconductor microcavities. The physics is governed by an effective spin-orbit coupling arising from TE/TM splitting, which dictates the polarization of edge states.
key_observables: Circular polarization ($S_3$), degree of elliptical polarization, and directional emission observed via $\sigma^+$ vs $\sigma^-$ pumping in both linear and gapped lattice geometries.
important_parameters: The TE-TM coupling strength ($\Omega_{TE-TM}$), the complex wavevector associated with evanescent fields ($\lambda_y$), and the lasing threshold power ($P_{th}$).
main_assumptions: SML is shown to be an intrinsic property arising solely from the exponentially localized nature of edge states, independent of external magnetic fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate SEM images of zigzag edges, simulated band structures showing opposite spin polarization for counter-propagating modes, and experimental maps demonstrating directional switching of emission based on pump helicity above lasing threshold.
paper_structure: The paper develops the argument by first establishing the theoretical origin of SML from TE-TM splitting in edge states. It then presents experimental evidence using polarimetry to confirm this locking in both normal and stretched honeycomb lattices, culminating in a demonstration of spin-controlled directional lasing.
why_interesting: This work provides an optical analogue for realizing robust chiral transport phenomena, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and condensed matter physics concerning topological edge states and spin-orbit coupling effects in artificial systems.

Spin-momentum entanglement.note: The core finding of spin-momentum locking (SML) in edge states—where the direction of propagation dictates the polarization/spin state ($\sigma^+$ vs $\sigma^-$)—is a direct manifestation and experimental realization of spin-momentum entanglement.

Spintronics.note: The study involves exciton-polaritons in semiconductor microcavities exhibiting spin-orbit coupling effects (TE/TM splitting) leading to polarization control ($\sigma^+$ vs $\sigma^-$ pumping), which falls directly under the quantum-optics interface with spin transport concepts.
